title.text: Why is it easy to test?

runs.text: Why is it easier to test a piece that only computes than one that reads or shows?
To test something that reads, you have to give it inputs; to test something that shows, you have to look at the screen. A pure function only needs its data.

justification.text: A pure function can be long; what matters is that it has no effects.

runs.text: Because with the same data it always gives the same and there is nothing to prepare.

justification.text: Calling it and comparing the result is enough, as in the table of cases in the lesson.

runs.text: Because the engine runs it faster.

justification.text: Speed does not change what has to be prepared to test it.
